subject: Next steps: local SDK sandbox + sample app plan for Lumina Health
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + local SDK sandbox plan

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary (30m call)
- Primary use case: clinical knowledge retrieval + summarization for internal care teams (private deployment concerns).
- Key constraints: must run in VPC, low-latency for short queries (~100–300ms target), embeddings stored in Pinecone (customer-managed).
- Must support: Python backend (FastAPI) + TypeScript frontend example, structured tool-calling for a medication-checker microservice, and reranker for candidate passages.

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) Sandbox deliverables (we'll provide):
   - Minimal Python sample that calls Redwood hosted API + local fallback wiring (redwood-sdk quickstart).
   - TypeScript sample app that shows streaming chat + tool call hook (open modal + call medication-checker).
   - Embedding example and reranker stub showing how to integrate Pinecone with our embeddings output.
2) Security/compliance: we attached a short questionnaire you mentioned; can you confirm scope for on-prem vs VPC?
3) Timeline: aim for a 5-working-day sandbox that you can spin up locally (we'll provide a single-package archive and a one-command Docker dev flow).

Blocked items from your side
- Access preference for Pinecone namespace and test API key (we can use a sample if you prefer).
- Any strict network egress rules for the dev box (to validate fallback behavior).

I've attached a concise quickstart checklist that includes the two sample apps and local testing steps. Karthik and Neha are on copy to scope the implementation details. If that plan looks good I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to kick off the sandbox.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart-checklist.pdf (1 page — prioritized steps)

From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@luminahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + local SDK sandbox plan

Thanks Stephanie — that recap is spot on. A few clarifications from our infra team (Daniel copied):

Tech constraints
- Pinecone: we'll provide a dev namespace and key, but production will be in our VPC-hosted vector DB. For the sandbox it's OK to use hosted Pinecone.
- Egress: dev VMs must be able to reach redwood inference endpoints over TLS (443); no other outbound except package registries.
- Tool calling: medication-checker service will run as a local container that accepts a JSON payload and returns structured JSON (status, interactions). We need the SDK sample to demonstrate the tool-calling flow and a safe fallback when the tool returns error codes.
- Reranker: we use a lightweight BERT-based reranker today; can you show pseudocode for a rerank step that uses Redwood embeddings + our reranker scores?

Deliverables we want in the sandbox
- Python: FastAPI example + tests (run with pytest) showing embedding -> vector search -> rerank -> structured-tool-call.
- TypeScript: small React app with streaming chat plus a UI for tool invocation (mocked local container).
- README that includes how to switch from hosted demo keys to an on-prem config (ENV vars or a single config file).

Security doc: attached (filled with preliminary answers). We'll review the checklist and get you the Pinecone test key.

If you can get us a PR branch or a zip by next Wednesday (5/25) we can try the local pilot the following week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Reynolds
VP Product | Lumina Health
alex.reynolds@luminahealth.com

Attachment: lumina-security-questions.pdf

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + local SDK sandbox plan — asks from Lumina (see below)

Karthik / Neha — forwarding Alex's responses and the filled security doc. Key asks:
- Provide two sample apps: FastAPI flow (embed -> search -> rerank -> tool call) and TS React streaming chat with tool UI.
- Demonstrate a pattern for safe tool-calling + error fallback handling.
- Include small snippet showing how to plug in an external reranker (pseudocode ok).

Proposed split:
- Karthik: take the Python sample and the reranker pseudocode + pytest smoke tests. Add a Dockerfile and a one-liner dev run.
- Neha: TypeScript React app with streaming + tool call UI + README for switching config to on-prem. Also include instructions for mocking the medication-checker container.

I'll own packaging the deliverable, the one-page checklist, and the walkthrough scheduling. Can you both confirm capacity to deliver a draft package by 5/25? If not, call out what you need.

Thanks — Steph

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: local SDK sandbox + sample app plan for Lumina Health

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We've scoped a minimal deliverable and confirmed we can hit a 5/25 draft. Summary of what we'll hand over by 2027-05-25: 

1) Python sample (redwood-python-sample)
   - FastAPI app (app.py) demonstrating: call to Redwood text generation, embeddings upload example, vector search integration sample (# uses Pinecone client), reranker pseudocode function, and a tool-caller client that POSTs to a local container endpoint with robust error handling (retries + safe fallback).
   - Dockerfile + docker-compose for local dev (medication-checker mocked as a tiny Flask container).
   - pytest smoke tests that validate the end-to-end happy path and a forced-tool-error path.

2) TypeScript sample (redwood-ts-chat)
   - React app with streaming chat UI using the Redwood JS SDK (streaming example).
   - Example of tool invocation: UI triggers a modal payload, sends to Redwood via function-calling hook; on tool error falls back to a text-only summary.
   - README with instructions to swap demo keys for on-prem config (ENV vars: REDWOOD_API_URL, REDWOOD_API_KEY, PINECONE_NAMESPACE).

3) Docs + checklist
   - One-page quickstart checklist (attached to Steph's email).
   - Developer notes for integrating an external reranker: simple glue code snippet and where to plug in.

Next steps
- We'll upload a draft zip + a GitHub branch (private) to the Drive link Stephanie shared, and give Lumina a short video walkthrough (15 min) on 5/26 (optional — confirm preferred time).

Alex — is 5/26 for a 15-minute walkthrough OK? Prefer morning Pacific.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
